title: The program's write path
body:
## Goal
Dev flow can write on GitHub as the app, through a write path that is typed so that only a key narrowed for its purpose can be used: a push key for a worker, opening a pull request, commenting, labelling, opening an issue and merging. The owner's own actions stay on his linked token, and every read stays read only.

## Context
- The feature issue, "Dev flow: one card, end to end": "The program writes on GitHub as the app".
- The spec, round 3: "The program acts on GitHub as a GitHub App", "What the owner does from the page is recorded on GitHub as done by him", "Developer and reviewer share the app's identity"; round 4: "How code reaches a worker and comes back": the worker's key lasts an hour, reaches one repository, and can only read and push code; "The worker's key cannot change a project's CI workflows" under "Clarified after the builder check".
- What part 1 built and this slice must keep true: "Its own keys can only read" under "GitHub", "Acting from the page", and the security entries "The app holds write access to code, and the program's own keys never use it" and "Writes are made only with a linked user's token, and the code makes the other impossible", all in `devflow/docs/devflow-architecture.md`. The code: `devflow/src/DevFlow/CodeHost/GitHub/InstallationTokens.cs`, `GitHubCodeHost.Writes.cs`, `Writes.cs`, `ICodeHost.cs`, the fake's `FakeCodeHost.Writes.cs`, and the tests `InstallationTokenTests`, `GitHubWriteTests` and `IlScan.cs`.
- `contracts/github/`: GitHub's answers recorded once, against which the adapter is tested. No automated test touches GitHub.
- GitHub's documentation, to be read when this slice is built and its answers recorded: creating an installation access token with `permissions` and `repository_ids`; creating a pull request, `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls`; creating an issue comment; adding and removing labels on an issue; creating an issue; merging a pull request with `sha` and `merge_method`.

## Acceptance
- `AppWriteTokenTests.OnlyTheIssuerMakesOne` (xUnit, the compiled code scanned as `IlScan.cs` does): `AppWriteToken` has no public constructor and is made only in `InstallationTokens`.
- `AppWriteTokenTests.EachPurposeAsksForExactlyItsPermissions` (xUnit, stub handler): the request body for push is `contents: write` and `metadata: read`; for posting, `issues: write`, `pull_requests: write` and `metadata: read`; for merging, `contents: write`, `pull_requests: read` and `metadata: read`; each with `repository_ids` holding the one repository.
- `AppWriteTokenTests.NoPurposeAsksForWorkflows` (xUnit): no request ever names `workflows`.
- `InstallationTokenTests` still passes: every read token is read only.
- `ReadPathTests.TheReadingCodeCannotReachAWriteToken` (xUnit, the compiled code scanned): nothing under `Reading/` or `Runner/`, and no read method of the adapter, references `AppWriteToken` or a write purpose.
- `GitHubAppWriteTests.EachWriteMatchesGitHubsDocumentedForm` (xUnit, stub handler, against recorded answers): open a pull request, comment on an issue or pull request, add a label, remove a label, open an issue, merge with `sha` and `merge_method` `merge`; their failures read as the interface's results.
- `FakeAppWriteTests.TheFakeRecordsWhoWroteWhat` (xUnit): each write in the fake is recorded as the app's, with its purpose, so a test can tell the app's writes from the owner's.
- `CommentTests.NothingIsEverWrittenAsTheApp` is renamed and narrowed to what it guards: the owner's actions from the waiting list are never written as the app.
- `ContractTests` covers the new recorded answers.
- Screenshots: none.

## Tasks
- [ ] Add `AppWriteToken` and the purposes to the installation token issuer, with their tests.
- [ ] Add the app's writes to `ICodeHost`, the GitHub adapter and the fake, with the recorded answers and their tests.
- [ ] Extend the scans so the read paths cannot reach a write token, and narrow the part 1 test that said nothing is written as the app.
- [ ] Write the docs named in Settled.

## Settled
- **Two write paths, each typed.** The owner's writes from the page take a `UserAccessToken`, as today, and nothing changes there. The program's own writes take an `AppWriteToken`: a type of its own, with no public constructor, made only by `InstallationTokens.ForWrite(repository, purpose)`. An installation's read token is a string and a `UserAccessToken` is another type, so neither can be passed where an `AppWriteToken` is wanted, and the compiler keeps the paths apart.
- **Three purposes, each narrowed in the request for the key:**
  - `Push`: `contents: write`, `metadata: read`. Handed to a worker to fetch and push code, see "Handing out work and the brief". It cannot comment, or touch an issue or a label. It can push to any branch of the one repository, `main` included, and GitHub puts merging a pull request under Contents too, so it could merge through the API. The spec said the worker's key "cannot merge"; that is not so on GitHub, and there is no narrower permission. It is accepted as the spec accepted a push to `main`: `main` is watched, and anything landing there that Dev flow did not merge stops the project, see "Watching main". The architecture doc records the correction.
  - `Post`: `issues: write`, `pull_requests: write`, `metadata: read`. Opening a pull request, commenting, labelling, opening an issue.
  - `Merge`: `contents: write`, `pull_requests: read`, `metadata: read`. Merging only.
  No purpose asks for `workflows`, so no key Dev flow makes can change a project's CI.
- **The app's writes on the interface:** `OpenPullRequest(token, repository, head, base, title, body)`, `CommentOnIssue(token, repository, number, body)` (an issue or a pull request), `AddLabel` and `RemoveLabel(token, repository, number, label)`, `OpenIssue(token, repository, title, body, labels)`, and `MergeAsApp(token, repository, number, commit)`, a merge commit with `sha` set, so a moved head is refused by GitHub. Each answers its value or the interface's failures. Nothing is retried inside the adapter.
- **The fake** implements every write, records each with who made it, the app with its purpose or a user, and keeps a git repository per fake repository: a bare repository in a temporary folder per fake world, whose `file://` address the fake answers as the clone address, so a worker in a test can fetch and push for real.
- **A push key leaves Dev flow** only inside a job's answer or a fresh-key answer to the worker holding that job, see "Handing out work and the brief". It is kept in memory only, never stored.
- **The GitHub App needs Issues at write level** from now on. The owner changes it on GitHub and approves it on each installation; `devflow/README.md`'s "Registering the GitHub App" lists it.
- Dependencies: none new.
- Docs to change in this pull request: `devflow/README.md`, "The code host" and "Registering the GitHub App", gains the writes and the new permission. `devflow/docs/devflow-architecture.md` changes "Its own keys can only read" to say the program's own reads stay read only and its writes go through `AppWriteToken`, and its security section replaces "The app holds write access to code, and the program's own keys never use it" with: the program writes as the app through a second typed path; each key is narrowed to one purpose and one repository; no key can change workflows; the push key can reach `main`, which is watched. The entry "Writes are made only with a linked user's token" is narrowed to the owner's actions from the page, and says why the program's own writes are the app's: what the program does is marked as the app's on GitHub, so it is traced back to a card and a run, anti goal 8.

## Out of scope
- Using these writes: the later slices of this part and part 3.
- Watching `main`: "Watching main".

## Risk
high, it is the first time Dev flow can write code and merge without the owner, and it replaces part 1's guarantee that the program never writes.
